06/13.05.2024 Heard Mr. Rajeeva Sharma, learned senior counsel appearing for the
petitioner, Mr. Someshwar Roy, learned counsel for the State and Mr. Tapan Kumar Mishra, learned
counsel for the informant.
2.

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Saria P.S. Case No.124/2023,
registered for the alleged offence under Sections 498A, 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
pending in the Court of the learned C.J.M., Giridih.

3.  Mr. Sharma, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the husband of the deceased and now charge- sheet has been submitted under Section 306 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
He submits that mother-in-law of the deceased has been granted regular bail by the High Court.

He further submits that the petitioner is innocent and there are general and omnibus allegations against all the accused persons and in view of that, privilege of anticipatory bail may kindly be provided to the petitioner.
4.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer on the ground that the petitioner is the husband and there is direct allegation against the petitioner.

5. Learned counsel for the informant submits that the allegations are there and the petitioner is the husband and even regular bail application of the father-in-law of the deceased has been rejected by the High Court.
He submits that even in postmortem, antemortem injury was found on the body of the deceased.

6. The petitioner is the husband of the deceased and there are allegations against the accused persons of demanding dowry and it has been pointed out that even injury was found on the body of the deceased at the time of postmortem.
Prima facie, the case of instigation is made out.
Further, the mother-in-law has been granted regular bail and in identical situation, the prayer for regular bail of father-in-law has been rejected by this Court.
7. In the attending facts and circumstances of the case, I am not inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Accordingly, the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner is rejected.
8. However, if the petitioner surrenders before the learned Court, the learned Court will pass the order in accordance with law without prejudiced to this order.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Ajay/
